Subject: Acme — Post-call TCO recap and next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — good to understand the immediate goals and constraints. Below is a short recap from our side and the suggested next steps. I focused this on the cost/TCO levers we discussed so the procurement and finance teams have a clear starting point.

TL;DR
- Primary goal: get LLM-based summarization & search into production for support use cases with predictable monthly spend <= $35k.
- Main pain points: token cost variability (spiky traffic), expensive peak provisioning, and quality regressions when trying smaller models.
- Recommended next step: 45m technical deep-dive + walk-through of the attached TCO model (redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx).

What we heard
- Workload: ~120k API calls/day today (peak 2-3x), average prompt length ~280 tokens, expected growth to ~250k calls/day in 6 months.
- SLOs: 95th pct latency target ~300ms for the primary summarization route.
- Budget: finance target ~ $30-35k/month for inference cost (excluding infra ops).

Primary cost drivers we identified
1) Tokens per call: Avg 280 in + 240 generated = ~520 tokens/call -> ~26M tokens/day at 50% prompt/generation split.
2) Peak provisioning needed for spikes (2-3x) - naive provisioning raises unit costs.
3) Model selection: larger models with higher per-token cost currently used for highest quality paths.

Redwood levers to hit target (what we'll demo)
- Batching & continuous batching: reduces per-token overhead during high throughput; expect 20-40% token-cost reduction for your burst profile.
- Prefix/KV caching: reuse embeddings/KV for repeated prefixes and common prompts - big wins for support templates; can cut token compute by 15-30% depending on repeat rate.
- Model routing & quantization: route low-risk flows to a smaller, quantized variant and fall back to higher-cost models for edge cases; typical blended cost improvement 25-45%.
- Autoscaling + burst policies: use reserve capacity for baseline and burst to hosted pools for peaks to avoid constant overprovisioning.

Example quick TCO snapshot (ballpark)
- Current (naive): est $48k/mo inference (1M tokens = $X - detailed calc in attachment).
- With batching + caching + routing: est $28-32k/mo (within your target range).

Attachments
- redwood-tco-modeling.xlsx (detailed token calc & scenarios)
- acme-mop-map.pdf (recommended model-to-route mapping)

Next steps
1) Can you confirm: current avg tokens/call (prompt + response) and expected % of calls that are repeatable templates?
2) I'll schedule a 45m technical deep-dive with Rafael to walk the TCO model and demo batching/caching. Options: Tue 11/24 10a PT, Wed 11/25 9a PT, or Thu 11/26 1p PT. Which works?
3) I'll surface security/compliance checklist and SOC2 snapshot for procurement in the follow-up.

Happy to adjust the model once you confirm the token counts - attached has placeholders.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
